verdicts.note: Clinical review of elective oocyte cryopreservation for deferred childbearing.
No abstract. Parents' attitudes to IVF cost and coverage.
Lifestyle factors and fertility rates. B.4's.
Letter responding to Hoorens et al. / the RAND report on whether ART can offset population ageing. A published contest of an arm-1 claim — chase both sides at full text.
COVID-19 and US MAR live-birth rates. A supply interruption used as a shock — the closest thing in the frame to an access experiment on the arm-1 series.
No abstract, no venue. 'Role of Insurance Mandate' — probably a commentary.
Bongaarts-Feeney tempo adjustment mechanics. A.11's.
ART framed as national demographic policy — the policy-facing version of arm 1's claim, and the framing v5 inherits.
Unrealized fertility plans in Hungary.
Elective OVARIAN TISSUE cryopreservation for age-related decline — a distinct technology from oocyte freezing, same elective indication.
Health and fertility expectations. D.3.a-adjacent.
German fertility trend commentary.

**PREGNANCY AFTER DROPPING OUT OF TREATMENT, Japan.** This is arm 1's counterfactual measured directly: how often women who stop treatment conceive anyway. Every ART birth counted as additional assumes this number is zero. Priority full-text — it is the single most useful record found so far for bounding the upper bound.
Nine scenarios for the future MAR share of Italian births to 2050.
Age curve of biological capacity from natural-fertility populations — another P4 parameter source.
No abstract. Women's awareness and perceptions of delay.
ART's contribution to multiple births and hospital days, US 1996. Arm-1 SHAPE with A.12's outcome — the clearest illustration that the arm field and the cell field are orthogonal.
Brief review of age-fertility knowledge.
Pison, Monden & Smits 2015 — A.12's OWN ANCHOR, surfacing in A.17's frame. Confirms the two chapters' neighbourhoods overlap exactly where the scope-freeze said they would.
Eurobarometer childbearing preferences.
Editorial on insurance for iatrogenic infertility after cancer treatment. Wall 5's medical half, and it explicitly contrasts iatrogenic with 'elective' — useful for the indication boundary.
No abstract. Trends, causes and consequences of advanced-age parenthood.
Advocacy commentary on warning women about age-related decline.
Population-based UK/Denmark survey of fertility awareness — larger and better sampled than the student surveys that dominate this cell.
Medical students, three European countries.
Opinion piece on encouraging earlier childbearing.

Austria: LATE FERTILITY INTENTIONS RISE OVER TIME WHILE CHANCES OF A LATE BIRTH REMAIN LOW. The belief-behaviour gap measured against a realized outcome rather than an attitude — the P6 record with the most content so far.
Late parenthood and childlessness by education, France.
Intergenerational mobility and completed fertility, Poland.
Parental divorce and adult children's fertility. A.19/D.2's.
Untitled-beyond-'Fertility' book chapter with no abstract.
Quantum/timing/variance decomposition of first births.
The economics of IVF and the case for PUBLIC FUNDING. Policy-facing; whether it reports a birth response is the full-text question.

**PDR SYSTEMATIC REVIEW of the (quasi-)experimental literature on whether policies raise fertility.** A channel-1 record for the whole review, and the natural place to check whether ART-access studies have already been collected and appraised by someone else.
Argues class disparities in treatment persist BEYOND financial access — bears on whether price is the binding constraint arm 2 assumes it is.
Women's views on funding egg freezing.
Postponement and realized fertility among highly educated US women 1920-1986 — the observed counterpart to P4's simulations.
Complementary and alternative medicine for uninsured infertility patients.
Psychosocial adjustment of involuntarily childless women.
Infertility coverage for physician trainees specifically.
Undergraduate journal review of treatment efficacy.
Leridon's 1978 monograph on natural fertility components — the intellectual root of P4 but not an A.17 record.
ART multiple-birth trends, US 1997-2000.
Qualitative interviews on postponement, Sweden.

**RESIDENTIAL PROXIMITY TO A FERTILITY CLINIC against treatment uptake.** The second genuine P2 record in the frame and the first on the distance margin — the recon probe's supply-side cell was almost entirely clinical noise, so this cell is thin but not empty.
Serbian medical students.

**RCT PROTOCOL (FertStart, Singapore): fertility-education interventions with CHILDBEARING among the outcomes.** If the trial reports births, it is the only record in P6 that reaches the BEHAVIOUR side experimentally. Chase the results publication, not the protocol.
No abstract. Childlessness convergence by education.
PGT outcomes under private vs PUBLIC funding periods. A funding-regime change with a per-cycle outcome — Wall 1 by outcome, arm-2 by exposure.
Erratum record. The shadow gate would refuse this as a seed; here it is simply not a work.
Dissertation on Canadian women's knowledge of delay consequences.
Mandates against DONOR-OOCYTE utilisation, 39,338 SART cycles. Large, and donor oocytes are the treatment margin most able to overcome age-related decline — the mechanism P4 models.
Duplicate-shaped record of the 'conflicting clocks' commentary.
Textbook chapter on involuntary childlessness. Note it lists ADOPTION and GIVING UP TREATMENT as sections — the substitution margins arm 1 assumes away.
NEJM 2013, Kulkarni et al. — the standard decomposition of US multiple births into ART and NON-ART ovulation induction. A.12 needs this; it is the target the batch-3 letter was arguing about.
Experimental test of a fertility-education website on knowledge AND beliefs about timing. Manipulation on the belief side; still not behaviour.
Time-to-pregnancy trends in Sweden. B's.
Critique of South Korean pronatalist use of reproductive technology.
Receipt of medical help to conceive among racial and sexual minority women — access on a non-price margin.
Mortality among infertile men.
